questions.question: During the reign of which of the following Mauryan kings, the Kalinga War was fought?
questions.solution:
The Kalinga War was fought in 261 BC. After witnessing the massive bloodshed, Ashoka embraced Buddhism and abandoned the policy of physical occupation in favor of cultural conquest.
  • It is mentioned in Ashoka's 13th Rock Edict.
  • Kalinga is the ancient name of coastal Odisha.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first Indian to be admitted to the Indian Civil Service in British India?
questions.solution:
Satyendranath Tagore became the first Indian to join the Indian Civil Service in 1863.
  • He was the elder brother of Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore.
  • The ICS was previously known as the Covenanted Civil Service.

questions.question: Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the _________, an organisation that attempted to reform Hinduism.
questions.solution:
The Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in 1875 in Bombay.
  • His famous slogan was 'Back to the Vedas'.
  • He wrote the book Satyarth Prakash to spread his teachings.

questions.question: Radio broadcasting started in India in 1923 by the _____.
questions.solution:
Radio broadcasting in India was initiated by the Radio Club of Bombay in June 1923.
  • This was followed by the setting up of the Indian Broadcasting Service.
  • It later became All India Radio (AIR) in 1936 and was renamed Akashvani in 1957.

questions.question: Who among the following Gupta rulers was hailed as 'Indian Napoleon' because of his military achievements?
questions.solution:
Samudragupta was called the 'Indian Napoleon' by historian V.A. Smith due to his extensive military conquests.
  • Information about his reign is found in the Prayag Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar inscription) composed by his court poet Harishena.
  • He was a great patron of art and was depicted on coins playing the Veena.

questions.question: Gandhi-Irwin pact was signed in which year?
questions.solution:
The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on March 5, 1931, between Mahatma Gandhi and Lord Irwin.
  • It led to the suspension of the Civil Disobedience Movement.
  • It paved the way for Congress participation in the Second Round Table Conference in London.

questions.question: Who among the following Greek rulers sent Megasthenes to the court of Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.solution:
Seleucus Nicator, a Greek ruler (general of Alexander), sent his ambassador Megasthenes to the court of Chandragupta Maurya.
  • Megasthenes wrote the famous book 'Indica', which describes the Mauryan administration and society.
  • He was the first foreign envoy to India.

questions.question: In which year was Jhansi annexed by Lord Dalhousie under the policy Doctrine of Lapse?
questions.solution:
Jhansi was annexed in 1854 by Lord Dalhousie using the Doctrine of Lapse.
  • Under this policy, if an Indian ruler died without a natural male heir, the kingdom passed to the British.
  • Other states annexed included Satara (1848), Sambalpur (1850), and Nagpur (1854).

questions.question: ______ spent a lot of time at Harshavardhana's court and left a detailed account of what he saw.
questions.solution:
The Chinese pilgrim Xuan Zang (Hiuen Tsang) visited India during the reign of Harshavardhana.
  • He stayed for about 15 years and left a detailed account titled Si-yu-ki.
  • He studied at the Nalanda University during his stay.

questions.question: Who among the following founded the Shunga dynasty?
questions.solution:
The Shunga Dynasty was founded by Pushyamitra Shunga in 185 BC.
  • He was the Commander-in-Chief (Senapati) of the last Mauryan king, Brihadratha, whom he assassinated.
  • He was a staunch follower of Brahminism and performed Ashvamedha sacrifices.

questions.question: To defend the Khalifa's temporal powers, a Khilafat Committee was formed in Bombay in ______.
questions.solution:
A Khilafat Committee was formed in Bombay in March 1919 to defend the temporal powers of the Khalifa.
  • The movement was led by the Ali brothers (Mohammad Ali and Shaukat Ali).
  • Mahatma Gandhi supported the movement to bring Hindus and Muslims together for a united national struggle.

questions.question:
चूंकि मौर्य साम्राज्य इतना बड़ा था, इसलिए अलग-अलग हिस्सों पर अलग-अलग शासन किया जाता था। ______ के आसपास के इलाकों पर सम्राट का सीधा नियंत्रण था।

Since the Maurya Empire was so large, different parts were ruled separately. The emperor had direct control over the areas around ______.
questions.solution:
In the Mauryan Empire, the Emperor had direct administrative control over the areas surrounding the capital city, Pataliputra.
  • Other regions were governed as provinces with capitals like Taxila and Ujjain.
  • Officials were appointed to collect taxes from farmers, herders, and traders in these areas.

questions.question: Ravikirti composed prashasti of which of following Chalukya rulers?
questions.solution:
Ravikirti was the court poet of the Chalukya King Pulakeshin II.
  • He composed the Aihole Inscription in Sanskrit.
  • The inscription describes the victory of Pulakeshin II over Harshavardhana on the banks of the Narmada.

questions.question: In which region did the Swadeshi Movement have the strongest impact on people?
questions.solution:
The Swadeshi Movement had its strongest impact in Bengal.
  • It started as a reaction against the Partition of Bengal in 1905 by Lord Curzon.
  • The movement emphasized the boycott of British goods and the use of Indian-made (Swadeshi) products.

questions.question: Awadh was annexed by the British in ______.
questions.solution:
Awadh was annexed by the British in 1856 on the grounds of 'maladministration'.
  • Lord Dalhousie carried out this annexation, which became a major cause of the 1857 Revolt.
  • Wajid Ali Shah was the last Nawab of Awadh at the time of annexation.

questions.question: The Rig Veda is a collection of ________ hymns.
questions.solution:
The Rig Veda is the oldest of the four Vedas and contains 1,028 hymns (Suktas).
  • It is divided into 10 books known as Mandalas.
  • The famous Gayatri Mantra is found in the 3rd Mandala of the Rig Veda.

questions.question: According to Megasthenes, the guards of Chandragupta rode _________ decorated with gold and silver during royal processions.
questions.solution:
According to Megasthenes, the royal guards of Chandragupta Maurya rode elephants decorated with gold and silver during processions.
  • He noted that the king was often surrounded by armed women for protection.
  • His accounts provide a glimpse into the grandeur of the Mauryan court.

questions.question: In which year did Congress and Muslim League signed the Lucknow pact?
questions.solution:
The Lucknow Pact was signed in 1916 between the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League.
  • It was significant for bringing the Moderates and Extremists back together within the Congress.
  • Ambika Charan Mazumdar presided over this historic Congress session.

questions.question: During the Chola period, muvendavelan and araiyar were titles of ______.
questions.solution:
In the Chola Empire, Muvendavelan (a peasant serving three kings) and Araiyar (chief) were titles given to rich landowners.
  • These titles were markers of respect and responsibility in the central state administration.
  • The Cholas were known for their highly organized local self-government.

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of the ‘Khudai Khidmatgars’ non-violent movement?
questions.solution:
Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, also known as Frontier Gandhi, founded the 'Khudai Khidmatgars' (Servants of God).
  • This was a non-violent movement that participated in the Civil Disobedience Movement.
  • The members were famously known as the 'Red Shirts'.

questions.question: Bastar Rebellion in central India broke out in ______.
questions.solution:
The Bastar Rebellion broke out in 1910 in present-day Chhattisgarh against British forest policies.
  • The rebellion was led by Gunda Dhur.
  • The local tribes protested against the reservation of forests which affected their traditional livelihoods.

questions.question: Who among the following was the last king of the Mauryan empire?
questions.solution:
Brihadratha was the last king of the Mauryan Empire.
  • He was assassinated by his own commander, Pushyamitra Shunga, in 185 BC.
  • His death marked the end of the Mauryan dynasty and the start of the Shunga dynasty.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first ruler of the Sunga dynasty?
questions.solution:
The Shunga dynasty was established by Pushyamitra Shunga.
  • He replaced the Mauryan Empire.
  • During his reign, the Stupa of Bharhut was extensively renovated.

questions.question: Which of the following acts passed by the Britishers disallowed Indians from possessing arms?
questions.solution:
The Arms Act of 1878 was passed during the viceroyalty of Lord Lytton.
  • It prohibited Indians from carrying or possessing arms without a license.
  • This was seen as a highly discriminatory move by the British against Indian citizens.

questions.question: Ashvaghosha who composed ‘Buddhacharita’ lived in the court of ______.
questions.solution:
Ashvaghosha, the author of the epic Buddhacharita, was a court poet of the Kushana king Kanishka.
  • He was a philosopher and poet who played a key role in the Fourth Buddhist Council.
  • Buddhacharita is a biography of Gautam Buddha written in Sanskrit.
